summary: US stocks rotated Tuesday: Dow +1.0% and Russell +1.8% while the Nasdaq-100 slipped 0.1% on AI-funding worries, and Netflix fell ~3-4% after hours on weak guidance. Oil whipsawed on Iran-deal headlines (Brent settled $108.79), the 10-year held near 5.11% with ~90% odds of a December Fed hike, and the dollar eased across the board.
events_next_24h: Wed (time tbc) GBP/EUR BoE Bailey and ECB Lagarde, Lane speak
Thu ~7:00am USD Tesla, IBM, Texas Instruments, Lam Research earnings (after US close)

NKD.why: Nikkei is down 5.5% in five days as AI-funding fears hit SoftBank and chip names, and US tech lagged again overnight; hedge funds are already near a crowded short (12th pct).
NKD.risk: A US chip rally on earnings or a squeeze of the crowded short would flip it.

NQ.why: Nasdaq-100 lagged a strong Dow as money rotated out of AI names, it is down 3.7% in five days, 10-year yields sit above 5.1% and Netflix fell after hours.
NQ.risk: Strong Tesla or chip earnings, or yields dropping below 5%, would flip it.

ES.why: S&P rose only 0.3% as Dow strength offset tech weakness, with 5%+ yields and hike pricing against it and rotation inside the index rather than broad selling.
ES.risk: A clean break in tech or a sharp fall in yields would set direction.

YM.why: Dow gained 1.0% as healthcare, financials and consumer names drew rotation flows out of tech, though 5%+ yields remain a headwind.
YM.risk: Another oil spike pushing yields higher, or the rotation reversing back into tech.

RTY.why: Small caps jumped 1.8% on rotation, but with 10-year yields above 5.1% and a December hike nearly priced the rate backdrop fights the move.
RTY.risk: Yields falling would make it bullish; a renewed yield jump bearish.

6J.why: USD/JPY at 158.2 is pinned by a wide US-Japan yield gap, but Tokyo's intervention warnings near 160 and Ueda's hike signals cap further yen weakness.
6J.risk: A break above 159-160 with no action would make it bearish; actual intervention bullish.

6E.why: Euro rose 0.2% as the dollar eased, but heavy Fed-hike pricing keeps rate support with the dollar and gives no clear euro driver.
6E.risk: A Fed hike priced out would turn it bullish; hawkish Fed talk bearish.

6B.why: Sterling led G10 overnight (+0.6%) after hawkish BoE comments, but UK CPI at 5pm Sydney can flip it either way.
6B.risk: A hot UK CPI print would support a bullish call; a soft one bearish.

6A.why: AUD/USD rose 0.3% to 0.70 on a softer dollar, but mixed risk mood and Asian equity weakness give no clear direction.
6A.risk: A broad risk-on rally in Asia would make it bullish; a tech sell-off bearish.

ZN.why: Hot September CPI and oil above $100 keep a December Fed hike ~90% priced and the 10-year above 5.1%, though long yields dipped Tuesday.
ZN.risk: An Iran deal that drops oil sharply would rally bonds.

GC.why: Gold fell a third straight day to about $4,124 as oil-driven yield rises revived Fed hike bets, though it has held above $4,100 all month.
GC.risk: A softer dollar extending or a geopolitical flare-up would lift it.

CL.why: Hormuz tanker attacks keep Brent near five-month highs, but Iran-deal headlines swing prices and trend funds are already max long, so a crowded side.
CL.risk: A confirmed US-Iran deal would drop it hard; more tanker hits would push it up.
